notes: Only 1 case x 1 run per configuration, so there is no variance data. Treat the deltas as directional.

Both failed baseline assertions are design-driven: 'REPO_GUIDE.md at repo root' tests the skill's naming convention, and 'did not execute repo code' tests the skill's read-only rule. On content accuracy (auth, data model, commands, tests, JWT secret) both runs scored 6/6, so those assertions don't discriminate on this small repo.

Baseline ran the code (npm ci, Postgres in Docker, server, tests) and so confirmed real findings: 7/27 unit tests fail from mock import order, lint fails, and nx injects .env but the built app doesn't. The with-skill run only suspected the test bug ('not verified').

The with-skill guide is about 2x longer with about 7x more file:line citations (141 vs 20), uses full repo-relative paths, and includes a Mermaid architecture diagram, an ER diagram and a 19-endpoint table. It was 97s faster and used ~8k more tokens.

The with-skill run surfaced 29 false positives from check_paths.py (URL routes, identifiers, gitignored paths, and an lstrip bug on dotfiles). These are fixed after the run; the re-check shows 0 false positives.
